# AGENTS.md

## Project

GridPlayer is a cross-platform PyQt5 desktop app for playing multiple videos side-by-side, backed by VLC. Python 3.10+, using `uv` and `just`.

## Hard boundaries

* **Do not create commits or push changes unless explicitly requested by the user.**
* **Compiled resources are generated.** `gridplayer/resources/` is generated by `just generate-resources` from the raw sources in `resources/`. Do not hand-edit it; regenerate after changing raw resources.
* **Translations are managed externally.** Do not modify `.ts`/`.qm` files, `scripts/translations/*`, or run any `just translations-*` recipe unless explicitly requested by the user.
* **Vendored VLC code:** `gridplayer/vlc_player/vlc.py` is vendored. Do not modify it.

## Setup & common commands

```bash
uv sync
uv run gridplayer
uv run pytest
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .
```

## Driving the real app

`tests/real_app` runs the real player offscreen, with VLC, driven through its
menus. Use it to see a change working or to chase a bug in the app, rather
than writing a harness of your own.

* Write a scenario (in your scratchpad for a one-off) and run it:

  ```bash
  uv run python -m tests.real_app.run path/to/scenario.py --out some/dir
  ```

  It prints each step as a line of JSON and leaves `report.json`, `app.log`
  and the screenshots in the folder. A scenario is `def scenario(d)`, with
  optional `SETTINGS`; the docstring of `run.py` has an example, and
  `driver.py` what `d` does: `open`, `wait_for_cell`, `act` (an action of
  `params/actions.py` by name), `menu` and `choose` (a generated menu),
  `wait_until`, `check`, `note`, `shot`, `through_modal`, `serve`,
  `fake_sponsorblock`.
* The media are made by ffmpeg into `build/test-media/` the first time; the
  docstring of `tests/real_app/media.py` says what there is: a folder and a
  list of clips, a file with chapters, two audio and two subtitle tracks and
  files to find beside it, a stream in three sizes and a dubbed one (serve
  those with `d.serve`).
* The scenarios in `tests/real_app/scenarios` are tests too: `just
  test-real-app` (`pytest -m real_app`), and a job of their own in CI. A plain
  `uv run pytest` leaves them out. A bug one shows goes in `KNOWN_BUGS` in
  `test_scenarios.py` until it is fixed.
* Each run sets `GP_USER_DATA_DIR` under its output folder, so settings,
  cookies and caches are isolated on Windows as well as Linux and macOS.
* What the driver already takes care of, should you go around it:
  * The app picks the xcb platform itself, whatever `QT_QPA_PLATFORM` says;
    set `gridplayer.params.env.QT_PLATFORM`.
  * Hardware video needs an X11 window: offscreen takes the `vlc_sw_sp`
    video driver.
  * Closing the player asks "do you want to save?", which nobody answers
    (set `playlist/unsaved_changes` to `discard`), and ends the process with
    `os._exit`.
  * The managers' context is `player._context`.
* What to know when writing a scenario:
  * Wait for state, not for time. Tracks, sizes and languages are listed
    only once a video has loaded, and choosing an audio file, a size or a
    language reloads it.
  * A seek takes a moment to land, and `time` is the old one until it has
    (`chapters.playing` already goes by where it is arriving): wait for the
    time before judging from it.
  * Streamlink reads only the default audio of an HLS stream; for dubs, set
    `streaming/resolver_priority` to `yt_dlp`.
  * Audio and subtitle files beside a video are offered only after "Detect
    Audio Files" / "Detect Subtitle Files".
  * VLC's clock steps back a few milliseconds on a track change.
  * `pkill -f` with a pattern that is also in your own command line kills
    your shell.

## Video block parts

`VideoBlock` (`gridplayer/widgets/video_block.py`) keeps the core: loading,
playback, seeking, rate and its Qt events. Everything else lives in a part, a
`VideoBlockPart` subclass in its own `video_block_<part>.py`, kept on the
block as an attribute: `status`, `bookmarker`, `view`, `chapters`,
`sponsorblock`, `subtitles`, `audio`, `loop`, `screenshot`, `recovery`,
`stream` and `navigation`.

* A part reaches its block through `self._block`. When moving a method into
  a part, every `self.x` that is the block's must become `self._block.x`. A
  bare `self` passed on (to a dialog, a signal, `ctx.commands`) has to become
  `self._block` too; a test with a `Mock` block will not notice.
* The `only_initialized` / `only_seekable` / ... guards in
  `video_block_guards.py` work on part methods as well; they ask the block.
* Commands name part methods with a dot: `("active", "navigation.next")`,
  `LOADING_COMMANDS` entries, `manual_seek("bookmarker.seek", i)`. An
  `("all", "x")` command emits `VideoBlocksManager.all_x`, which
  `VideoBlocksManager` connects to `vb.<part>.<method>` for each new block.
  `tests/test_dotted_commands.py` checks that every named command resolves.
* Parts are made in `VideoBlock.__init__` before `init_url_resolver()`,
  which connects to them. A new part goes there too, and into
  `_block_parts()` in `tests/conftest.py`.
* In tests, `mock_block_parts(block)` gives a `Mock(spec=VideoBlock)` its
  parts, and `is_block_command("part.method")` checks a command name. A part
  that makes a `QTimer(block)` cannot take a `Mock` as its parent: patch
  `gridplayer.widgets.video_block_<part>.QTimer`, or use a `QObject`
  stand-in.
* An exception raised inside a Qt slot aborts the whole test run ("Fatal
  Python error: Aborted"), not just the test.

## Settings dialogs

The Settings dialog and the Playlist window (`dialogs/playlist_settings.py`)
are built in code from two places, on the same index-and-pages shell
(`dialogs/paged_dialog.py`):

* `params/settings_fields/` says what a setting is: its kind of field,
  label, range, choices, tooltip, and the rules that grey it out or hide it
  (`enabled_when`, `shown_when`, `shown_if`, `unavailable`). One module per
  domain; `registry.FIELDS` has them all by key.
* `params/settings_pages.py` says where it is shown, the way `params/menu.py`
  lays out a menu: groups, pages, sections and rows naming settings by key.
  A `Slot("name")` is filled by `SettingsDialog._slot_<name>`, for what isn't
  a setting (buttons, the cookie list). `PLAYLIST_PAGE` and `VIDEO_PAGE` are
  the Playlist window's Playlist and New Videos pages too; its Bookmarks
  and Lists pages are made by their managers (`bookmarks_page`,
  `lists_page`), only once shown, and change as they go, Cancel putting
  them back.

A new setting needs a default in `settings.py`, a field, and a place on a
page; `tests/test_settings_fields.py` checks the three agree.
`widgets/settings_form.py` builds a page; `widgets/settings_editors.py` has
an editor for each kind of field.

Only the page owns display order. Field-definition tuples can be reordered
without moving controls. The registry tests require exact coverage of
editable defaults, excluding the explicitly listed internal settings.

`params/settings_bindings.py` maps setting keys to playlist, video-default
and grid attributes. It has no presentation imports. A setting saved with a
playlist also needs a binding and a model field. Serialization and session
settings use these mappings, never the UI field definitions.

`models/settings_draft.py` owns each field's original stored value, initial
display and pending edit or reset. `SettingsForm.persistence_result()` is
the saving contract for both dialogs: `SetValue` writes a value,
`ResetValue` removes it, and an absent key leaves storage alone. Availability
and layout belong to the form; dialogs apply the resulting operations.

Reset goes back to the factory default in the Settings dialog and to the
global setting in the Playlist window. A playlist keeps only its own values,
unless "Save all settings in the playlist" is on: then every value is its
own once saved (`PlaylistSettings.keep_all`). A setting saved at its
default is removed from the ini (`Settings().reset`), not written.

An untouched fallback, rounded or clamped display preserves its original
value. A reset captures the editor's actual display and restores the raw
default, even if it cannot be displayed exactly. A later edit supersedes
the reset. Playlist edits create explicit overrides, including an edit back
to the inherited display; a reset removes the override. Retired languages
are deliberately normalized to the current default instead of preserved.

In tests, reach a setting's widget with `dialog.widget("section/key")`, a
page with `dialog.pages["id"]` and its form with `dialog.forms["id"]`.

## Translatable strings

`pylupdate5` only extracts a string when it sees a literal context and a
literal text in the call itself. Anything else still translates at runtime if
the entry happens to exist, but never reaches translators.

* Always write `translate("Context", "Text")` (or `self.tr("Text")`) with
  string literals at the call site.
* Do not add wrapper helpers such as `_t(text)` / `_tr(text)`, and do not pass
  the context through a constant or variable.
* Do not put `tr()` / `translate()` inside f-strings; translate first, then
  format or concatenate.
* Do not call `translate()` at import time in modules loaded before
  `init_translator()` (see `tests/test_translation_timing.py`).
* A choice or toggle shown both in the menu (`params/actions.py`,
  `player/managers/active_block.py`) and in the settings form
  (`params/settings_fields/`) uses one context named after the setting
  (e.g. `Transform`, `When Finished`, `Playlist Settings`). Other menu strings
  use `Actions`; other settings form strings use `SettingsDialog`.

## Code style

* Follow the Ruff configuration in `pyproject.toml`.
* Tests live in `tests/`.
